description: Original advanced AI and Amazon PPC posts; both personal and company destination each once; no Metricool.

posts.text:
AI agents need stop conditions—not just better prompts.

An agent can call tools, search documents and retry actions repeatedly. That doesn't prove the result is correct. In production, I would define a maximum step count, a tool-use budget, argument validation and an escalation route before granting autonomy.

I evaluate agent systems across four dimensions:
• Was the chosen tool appropriate?
• Was the tool output interpreted correctly?
• Did the task finish successfully?
• What did a successful outcome cost?

An open-ended retry loop can be expensive without becoming more reliable. Reliable agents need explicit exit rules.

What stopping condition do you enforce in production?

#AIAgents #LLM #AIEngineering #AIAutomation #AgenticAI

When Amazon PPC spend rises but units stay flat, raising bids is rarely my first move.

I first separate the diagnosis into traffic quality, search-term intent, unit conversion and economics.

A campaign may generate more clicks while sending shoppers whose queries are only loosely related to the product. Even when CTR looks healthy, units per click can deteriorate.

The better comparison is between similar search terms and comparable time periods: spend, clicks, units, placement mix and contribution profit.

If the traffic mix has changed, fix relevance before increasing exposure. If relevance is stable but conversion is falling, inspect the offer and listing.

What do you audit first when spend increases without more units?

#AmazonPPC #AmazonAdvertising #AmazonPrivateLabel #Ecommerce #ConversionRate

High RAG answer quality begins before generation.

When a model produces an incorrect answer, teams often rewrite the prompt first. But a prompt cannot recover a missing source document.

I would evaluate retrieval recall, evidence grounding and task success as separate measurements. A high similarity score can hide failures involving exact product IDs, dates, versions or uncommon terminology.

That is why lexical search, semantic retrieval, metadata filters and reranking should be compared on representative tasks instead of selected because of popularity.

Before swapping the language model, ask: what evidence did the retriever actually supply?

Which layer causes most of your RAG failures?

#RAG #LLM #InformationRetrieval #AIResearch #MachineLearning

TACoS is a useful Amazon KPI, but TACoS is not contribution profit.

It measures advertising spend relative to total sales. It does not account for every fulfillment cost, return, margin difference or inventory constraint.

I would never optimize a mature brand solely toward a lower TACoS. The business question is whether the next advertising dollar generates profitable incremental unit demand.

For decision-making, I prefer a combined scorecard of spend, units sold, conversion, total sales, TACoS and contribution margin.

A low TACoS can still conceal a weak commercial outcome.

How do you distinguish advertising efficiency from actual profitability?
